the conspectus of sources is that the location of individual theses seems to be determined sometimes by the incidence of cognate subject matter in Recanati even when the direct source of the theses is in all likelihood not Recanati. Conclusio xxix, which was inspired by the Bahir, is a case in point. It treats of the proper application of the name MSPS and is located between two theses both of which treat of angels. It is certain that Pico read the Bahir: Scholem proved it beyond doubt.5 But of the three theses that reflect recognizable passages in the Bahir only one (Conclusio xxix) derives in all likelihood from the Bahir itself, whereas the other two might equally well derive from quotations of the Bahir in Recanati's Commentary on the Pentateuch. The Bahir is the penultimate piece in Cod. Vat. Ebr. 191. It is the earliest extant text of Kabbala proper.
